records.derivational_analysis: The Indo-Aryan source is located in the north-western IA area; dictionary glosses ‘hand, arm’ often refer to the whole upper limb.
records.evidence: inspection of CDIAL 6586 dōs- ‘forearm’ ... finds dui ‘forearm’ in two northwestern IA languages ... it is highly probable that we have found the origin of Br. dū
records.uncertainty: The source says ‘highly probable’ and identifies an areal source rather than a single immediate donor language.

records.derivational_analysis: A connection with CDIAL 5228 jihvā-, juhūi- is tempting, but reconstructive details and an immediate borrowing source remain elusive.
records.evidence: Repeated search has not yet found an origin ... for Br. dūi, duwi ‘tongue’. Tempting as would be some connection with CDIAL 5228 ... details and an immediate borrowing source still elude one.

page_notes: Page 446 concludes section 14 with a reassignment of Br. (h)ullī from DEDR 500 to DEDR 701, then presents section 15's probable Indo-Aryan etymology for Br. dū ‘hand, arm’. The references and footnotes are not independent lexical records except footnote 6's unresolved dūi/duwi ‘tongue’ etymology.
